newsitem.title: USA: Hearings urged on FAA staffing shortages.
newsitem.headline: Hearings urged on FAA staffing shortages.

text.p: Four members of Congress from New York said Wednesday that air traffic controller staffing shortages were jeopardising safety in the New York City area and around the country.
"Quite simply, our nation's air traffic control system is in crisis," the four Republicans said in a letter requesting a hearing on Federal Aviation Administration staffing levels.
The letter was signed by Sen. Alfonse D'Amato and Reps. Michael Forbes, Susan Molinari and Peter King.
They said there have been 24 incidents of aircraft coming dangerously close to each other in the New York area since last October.

"The FAA has not adequately addressed staff shortages which has threatened the ability of these controllers to effective cary out their duties. As such, the safety of the travelling public has been put in jeopardy," they said.
D'Amato said there were supposed to be 339 controllers at the New York Air Route Traffic Control Centre but it currently has only 308 on duty with only 230 of them fully qualified.
He said that on most days the centre was operating with 20 percent to 30 percent fewer controllers on duty than it was supposed to have.
The FAA has been trying to rebuilt its controller force since 14,000 controllers were fired for an illegal strike against the government in 1981.
